name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
notes: Lunar Module position. LROC elevation -1926 m (datum not confirmed); height to be taken from the terrain data. Plan V8 uses the older NSSDC value 0.67408, 23.47297 (only metres apart).

name: Apollo 12
notes: Lunar Module position. Longitude is 0-360 east (same point as -23.4219). Landing date still to fill from NSSDC table.

name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
notes: Lunar Module position. Longitude is 0-360 east (same point as -17.47194). Landing date still to fill from NSSDC table.

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)
notes: Lunar Module position. Landing date still to fill from NSSDC table.

name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
notes: Lunar Module position. NSSDC lists the landing as 20 Apr 1972 (US date); confirm the UTC date before filling.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
notes: Lunar Module position from the LROC 2016 coordinate update.

name: Chang'e-4 (Von Karman crater)
notes: Liu et al. 2019 (used by plan test V6); source elevation -5935 m. Alternative LROC stereo-DTM value: lat -45.4561, lon 177.5885 (https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1100), about 0.4 km away. Far side: Earth never visible.

name: SLIM (near Shioli crater)
notes: LROC position of the lander, elevation -912 m (datum not confirmed). JAXA target site (stated as ME): lat -13.31549, lon 25.24889 (https://global.jaxa.jp/press/2024/01/file/jaxa_doc01_20240125_e.pdf).

name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
notes: NASA/LROC value, 2 decimals, elevation 2579 m (datum not confirmed). Finer NAIF CLPS kernel value: lat -80.12759, lon 1.44587 (https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/pds/pds4/clps/clps_spice/spice_kernels/fk/clps_to2im_im1_v02.tf). Landed on a ~12 degree slope, about 1.5 km from the intended site.

name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
notes: Sensitivity check: results are robust to a 370 m position shift, so this is low priority. Still worth finding a primary NASA or LROC touchdown point. LROC intended site: lat -84.78, lon 29.13 (https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1401). Intuitive Machines says it landed about 250 m from the intended site, in a ~20 m crater.

name: Blue Ghost M1 (Mare Crisium)
notes: CHECK: this is the nominal target site, not a confirmed touchdown point. LROC rounds the actual landing to about 19 N, 62 E; look for the precise value at https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1400.

name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton-de Gerlache)
notes: Coordinates are Glaser 2014 EPSC spot 1 as listed in the plan (test V10). Cross-checks: Artemis 'site 001' at 89.45 S, 222.69 E (Boazman et al. 2022, https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/aca590) and ESA slide 89.4 S, 222.6 E (https://bsgn.esa.int/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/07-Moonlight_LCNS_S4I_2024_Javier-Ventura-Traveset.pdf). All within about 0.3 km. Sources name the neighbouring crater differently (de Gerlache in Glaser 2014, Henson in Boazman 2022). One wiki page lists 229.69 E, probably a typo.

name: Site 004 (Shackleton rim, Artemis III region)
notes: Primary source: Boazman et al. 2022, Planetary Science Journal 3:275, Fig. 1 caption and Section 1 (89.78 S, 204.27 E, also written 155.73 W). Site 004 was first defined from Clementine data (Bussey et al. 1999), re-examined as site 4 of Mazarico et al. 2011, and tagged 004 by NASA's 2020 Artemis plan. The paper does not state a coordinate frame, so MOON_ME is NOT confirmed. To get a frame-stated value, check Table 3 of Mazarico et al. 2011 (LOLA-based) or the PGDA 78 'Site 4' 5 m DEM. Shackleton crater centre per IAU Gazetteer is 89.67 S, 129.78 E (https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/5450); it is a shadowed crater, not a lander site. Older web pages that say 89.9 S, 0 E are wrong.

name: Malapert Massif (Artemis candidate region)
notes: Notional landing site near the summit that NASA specified in a 2023 Artemis III geology-team request (as reported by Kring 2025). Not a confirmed landing target.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (ISRO coordinates)
notes: CHECK: ISRO figure as quoted by Wikipedia and Indian press; confirm in the ISRO landing brochure (https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/pdf/Missions/LVM3/LVM3M4_Chandrayaan3_brochure.pdf). About 0.36 km from the LROC position (see chandrayaan3_lroc). Landing about 12:33 UTC.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (LROC coordinates)
notes: LROC position of the lander, elevation 532 m (datum not confirmed). Same lander as chandrayaan3_isro; keep both so the app can show the source gap.
